phrases.translation: O humanity! Fear your Lord, for the ˹violent˺ quaking at the Hour is surely a dreadful thing
phrases.explanation: The chapter opens by calling all humanity to be mindful of their Lord because the quake associated with the Hour will be terrifying. The warning is meant to awaken people before that event arrives. It places accountability at the center of the chapter and calls listeners to prepare through reverence and obedience.

phrases.translation: The Day you see it, every nursing mother will abandon what she is nursing, and every pregnant woman will deliver her burden ˹prematurely˺.
phrases.explanation: When the Hour's quake is seen, even a nursing mother will abandon what she is nursing, and a pregnant woman will deliver early. These images convey overwhelming shock and fear. The verse describes the upheaval as so severe that ordinary bonds and the expected course of pregnancy are disrupted.

phrases.translation: And you will see people ˹as if they were˺ drunk, though they will not be drunk;
phrases.explanation: People will appear drunk because of the terror, although they have not consumed anything. The comparison describes confusion and loss of composure during the quake, not actual intoxication. The scene shows how completely the Hour will overwhelm those who witness it and how unlike ordinary fear this event will be.

phrases.translation: but the torment of Allah is ˹terribly˺ severe
phrases.explanation: The cause of this terror is the severe punishment of Allah. The verse moves from visible confusion to its true source, warning that the event is not merely a natural disturbance. Its force calls people to take divine judgment seriously while they still have time to turn toward their Lord.

phrases.translation: ˹Still˺ there are some who dispute about Allah without knowledge, and follow every rebellious devil
phrases.explanation: Some people argue about Allah without knowledge and follow every rebellious devil. Their claims lack sound guidance, yet they give their direction to forces that lead away from truth. The verse warns against confident religious dispute built on ignorance and against allowing rebellious influences to shape one's beliefs.

phrases.translation: It has been decreed for such devils that whoever takes them as a guide will be misguided and led by them into the torment of the Blaze
phrases.explanation: The rebellious devil is destined to mislead whoever chooses to follow it and lead that follower toward the Blaze. The verse describes the consequence of taking such a guide, not an excuse that removes human responsibility. Choosing corrupt guidance has a destination, so people must consider whom they follow.

phrases.translation: O humanity! If you are in doubt about the Resurrection, then ˹know that˺ We did create you from dust, then from a sperm-drop, then ˹developed you into˺ a clinging clot ˹of blood˺, then a lump of flesh—fully formed or unformed—in order to demonstrate ˹Our power˺ to you.
phrases.explanation: The verse answers doubt about resurrection by recalling human creation: from dust, through a sperm-drop, a clinging clot, and a lump that may be formed or unformed. These stages show that life develops by Allah's will. The description invites people to see their own beginning as evidence of God's power to create again.

phrases.translation: ˹Then˺ We settle whatever ˹embryo˺ We will in the womb for an appointed term, then bring you forth as infants, so that you may reach your prime.
phrases.explanation: Allah settles an embryo in the womb for an appointed term and brings the child into the world. The account stresses that development and birth occur within a time God determines. Human life does not begin through independent power, and the child grows toward maturity only by the conditions Allah provides.

phrases.translation: Some of you ˹may˺ die ˹young˺, while others are left to reach the most feeble stage of life so that they may know nothing after having known much.
phrases.explanation: People's lifespans differ: some die young, while others reach a frail age when they may lose much of what they once knew. The verse reminds readers that strength and knowledge are temporary gifts. Aging is part of human dependence, and life remains under God's control from beginning to end.

phrases.translation: And you see the earth lifeless, but as soon as We send down rain upon it, it begins to stir ˹to life˺ and swell, producing every type of pleasant plant
phrases.explanation: The lifeless earth becomes active and produces plants when Allah sends rain. Its revival offers a visible comparison for resurrection: land that seems barren can become full of growth again. The verse connects human creation and the renewal of the earth as signs that God can restore life after death.

phrases.translation: That is because Allah ˹alone˺ is the Truth, He ˹alone˺ gives life to the dead, and He ˹alone˺ is Most Capable of everything
phrases.explanation: These signs show that Allah alone is the Truth, gives life to the dead, and has power over everything. The verse gathers the preceding examples of human development and renewed earth into a conclusion about God's authority. Resurrection is possible because the One who gives life is not limited by creation's present state.

phrases.translation: And certainly the Hour is coming, there is no doubt about it.
phrases.explanation: The Hour is certainly coming, and the verse removes doubt about its arrival. Its timing may be unknown to people, but its certainty is not in question. The preceding signs of life and renewal prepare the reader to accept that the promised final event will also occur.

phrases.translation: And Allah will surely resurrect those in the graves
phrases.explanation: Allah will resurrect those in the graves. Death is therefore not the end of human existence or accountability. The verse completes its warning by affirming that people will be restored for judgment, where their earthly choices will matter and they will answer to the One who created them.

phrases.translation: ˹Still˺ there are some who dispute about Allah without knowledge, guidance, or an enlightening scripture
phrases.explanation: Some people continue to dispute about Allah without knowledge, guidance, or an enlightening scripture. Their argument lacks both reliable evidence and revealed direction. The verse exposes the weakness of making claims about God while refusing the sources that could correct them, and prepares to describe the harm their pride causes.

phrases.translation: turning away ˹in pride˺ to lead ˹others˺ astray from Allah’s Way.
phrases.explanation: Turning away in pride, these disputants try to lead others away from Allah's Way. Their error affects more than their own belief because they invite others to follow it. The verse warns that opposition to guidance can become an active effort to divert people from the path God has made clear.

phrases.translation: They will suffer disgrace in this world, and on the Day of Judgment We will make them taste the torment of burning
phrases.explanation: They face disgrace in this world and burning torment on Judgment Day. The verse presents consequences in both worldly life and the Hereafter for those who persist in arrogant misguidance. Their status and claims cannot shield them from judgment, because Allah knows what they have chosen and whom they have influenced.

phrases.translation: ˹They will be told,˺ “This is ˹the reward˺ for what your hands have done. And Allah is never unjust to ˹His˺ creation.”
phrases.explanation: They are told that their suffering is the result of what they themselves did, while Allah is never unjust to His creation. The verse links punishment to human action and rejects the idea that God wrongs anyone. It calls people to take responsibility for their choices rather than blaming the One who judges fairly.

phrases.translation: And there are some who worship Allah on the verge ˹of faith˺: if they are blessed with something good, they are content with it;
phrases.explanation: Some people worship Allah on the edge of faith, remaining satisfied when good fortune comes. Their attachment is conditional: they accept religion while life goes as they want. The image warns against treating faith as a bargain that is kept only when it brings immediate comfort or worldly advantage.

phrases.translation: but if they are afflicted with a trial, they relapse ˹into disbelief˺, losing this world and the Hereafter. That is ˹truly˺ the clearest loss
phrases.explanation: When hardship comes, these people relapse into disbelief and lose both this world and the Hereafter. The verse calls this the clearest loss because their unstable devotion leaves them without the reward of faith and without secure worldly satisfaction. It urges believers to remain faithful through changing circumstances.

phrases.translation: They call besides Allah what can neither harm nor benefit them. That is ˹truly˺ the farthest one can stray
phrases.explanation: They call upon beings besides Allah that can neither harm nor benefit them. Such worship takes them far from the truth because it directs dependence toward powerless objects or beings. The verse measures spiritual distance by the failure to recognize that only Allah controls benefit, harm, and the response to prayer.

phrases.translation: They invoke those whose worship leads to harm, not benefit. What an evil patron and what an evil associate
phrases.explanation: They invoke what brings harm rather than benefit, choosing an evil patron and associate. The verse describes the result of turning to false powers: instead of protection, they lead their followers toward loss. Its wording exposes how misplaced devotion harms the worshipper, not the One who alone deserves worship.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do good into Gardens, under which rivers flow. Surely Allah does what He wills
phrases.explanation: Allah admits believers who do good into Gardens with rivers flowing beneath them. Their reward joins faith with righteous action and is granted by God's will. The verse contrasts their lasting honor with the loss described earlier and reminds readers that Allah decides the outcome according to His wisdom.

phrases.translation: Whoever thinks that Allah will not help His Prophet in this world and the Hereafter, let them stretch out a rope to the ceiling and strangle themselves, then let them see if this plan will do away with ˹the cause of˺ their rage
phrases.explanation: Commentators differ over whether the verse concerns Allah's help for the Prophet or provision for the impatient person. In either reading, it challenges anyone who thinks God's aid will not come and asks whether a desperate scheme can change His decree. The rope and self-strangling are a severe rhetorical rebuke, not advice to self-harm.

phrases.translation: And so We revealed this ˹Quran˺ as clear verses.
phrases.explanation: Allah has revealed the Quran as clear verses. Their clarity gives people guidance and evidence, rather than leaving them without a way to understand the message. The statement links revelation to the signs already described and calls listeners to consider what is presented to them.

phrases.translation: And Allah certainly guides whoever He wills
phrases.explanation: Allah guides whoever He wills. Guidance is ultimately in God's hands, though people are still addressed with revelation and held responsible for their response. The verse closes the thought by directing believers to seek God's guidance and not treat their own judgment as independent of Him.

phrases.translation: Indeed, the believers, Jews, Sabians, Christians, Magi, and the polytheists—Allah will judge between them ˹all˺ on Judgment Day. Surely Allah is a Witness over all things
phrases.explanation: Believers, Jews, Sabians, Christians, Magi, and polytheists will all face Allah's judgment on the Last Day. The verse names distinct communities without saying that human labels replace God's judgment. Allah knows every person and is witness over all things, so the final decision belongs to Him alone.

phrases.translation: Do you not see that to Allah bow down ˹in submission˺ all those in the heavens and all those on the earth, as well as the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, and ˹all˺ living beings,
phrases.explanation: All in the heavens and earth, including the sun, moon, stars, mountains, trees, and living beings, bow in submission to Allah. The verse describes creation as subject to its Maker, whether or not people recognize that submission. The natural world is not an independent power but belongs to God's order.

phrases.translation: as well as many humans, while many are deserving of punishment.
phrases.explanation: Many people also submit, while many others deserve punishment. The contrast distinguishes those who willingly worship Allah from those who reject Him, even though every human remains within His creation. The verse warns that human choice has consequences and that a person's rank is not secured simply by belonging to humanity.

phrases.translation: And whoever Allah disgraces, none can honour. Surely Allah does what He wills
phrases.explanation: Whoever Allah disgraces cannot be honored by anyone, because His will prevails. The statement emphasizes that worldly status cannot reverse God's judgment. Allah is not constrained by human preferences, and His decisions rest on knowledge and authority beyond what people can control, prevent, or override.

phrases.translation: These are two opposing groups that disagree about their Lord: as for the disbelievers, garments of Fire will be cut out for them and boiling water will be poured over their heads
phrases.explanation: The verse describes two opposing groups disputing about their Lord and begins with the fate of the disbelievers. Garments of fire and boiling water portray the severity of their punishment. The image warns that rejecting God is not a harmless disagreement, since the dispute will have consequences in the Hereafter.

phrases.translation: melting whatever is in their bellies, along with their skin
phrases.explanation: The boiling water melts what is inside the disbelievers and their skin. This graphic description shows how severe the punishment in Hell is and leaves no comfort in the body. The verse continues the previous warning, making clear that the rejection of truth has consequences beyond mere argument or temporary discomfort.

phrases.translation: And awaiting them are maces of iron
phrases.explanation: Iron maces await the people being punished in Hell. The image adds to the account of their suffering and shows that this punishment is not easy to evade. It follows the description of boiling water and emphasizes the terrible outcome faced by those who rejected the warning.

phrases.translation: Whenever they try to escape from Hell—out of anguish—they will be forced back into it, ˹and will be told,˺ “Taste the torment of burning!”
phrases.explanation: Whenever they try to escape Hell in anguish, they are forced back and told to taste the punishment of burning. The verse depicts the hopelessness of trying to flee after judgment has come. Its warning is meant for people now, while repentance and a change of direction are still possible.

phrases.translation: ˹But˺ Allah will surely admit those who believe and do good into Gardens, under which rivers flow,
phrases.explanation: Allah admits believers who do good into Gardens with rivers flowing beneath them. The reward is described as a secure place granted to those who combine faith and righteous action. The image of flowing rivers conveys abundance and life, in contrast with the fire and anguish described for the other group.

phrases.translation: where they will be adorned with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing will be silk
phrases.explanation: In the Gardens, believers will wear bracelets of gold and pearls and garments of silk. These adornments portray honor and delight in the Hereafter. Their reward is not earned by status or wealth in this life, but is granted by Allah to those who believed and did good.

phrases.translation: for they have been guided to the best of speech, and they have been guided to the Commendable Path
phrases.explanation: The believers have been guided to the best speech and the praiseworthy path. The verse explains their honor by pointing to the guidance they received and followed. Their way is commendable because it leads toward obedience to Allah, and their words reflect the truth rather than the false claims of those who reject Him.

phrases.translation: Indeed, those who persist in disbelief and hinder ˹others˺ from the Way of Allah and from the Sacred Mosque—which We have appointed for all people, residents and visitors alike—
phrases.explanation: Those who persist in disbelief and hinder people from Allah's Way and the Sacred Mosque are warned. The sanctuary is appointed for all people, residents and visitors alike. The verse condemns blocking access to this place of worship and rejects the idea that it belongs only to a privileged local group.

phrases.translation: along with whoever intends to deviate by doing wrong in it, We will cause them to taste a painful punishment
phrases.explanation: Whoever intends to commit wrongdoing in the Sacred Mosque is also threatened with painful punishment. The warning reaches beyond completed acts to a deliberate intent to violate the sanctuary. It emphasizes the seriousness of wrongdoing in a place set apart for worship and calls people to approach it with reverence.

phrases.translation: And ˹remember˺ when We assigned to Abraham the site of the House,
phrases.explanation: Allah assigns Abraham the site of the House, the sanctuary that becomes a center of worship. The verse presents its location and purpose as established by divine instruction, not by human invention. This setting prepares for the commands about keeping the House devoted to Allah alone.

phrases.translation: ˹saying,˺ “Do not associate anything with Me ˹in worship˺ and purify My House for those who circle ˹the Ka’bah˺, stand ˹in prayer˺, and bow and prostrate themselves
phrases.explanation: Abraham is told not to associate anything with Allah and to purify the House for those who circle it, pray, bow, and prostrate. The sanctuary is to be dedicated to worship, not idols or rival powers. The listed acts show the different ways pilgrims and worshippers honor Allah there.

phrases.translation: Call ˹all˺ people to the pilgrimage. They will come to you on foot and on every lean camel from every distant path
phrases.explanation: Abraham is commanded to call people to pilgrimage, and they will arrive on foot or riding lean camels from distant routes. The verse portrays the pilgrimage as an invitation extended far beyond one nearby community. Their journeys converge on the House in response to God's command and in shared worship.

phrases.translation: so they may obtain the benefits ˹in store˺ for them,
phrases.explanation: Pilgrims come to obtain benefits Allah has placed in pilgrimage. These may include spiritual and communal good, though the verse does not reduce the pilgrimage to worldly advantage. The phrase presents the rites as beneficial to those who answer the call and make the journey with devotion.

phrases.translation: and pronounce the Name of Allah on appointed days over the sacrificial animals He has provided for them.
phrases.explanation: Pilgrims pronounce Allah's name on appointed days over sacrificial animals He has provided. The verse links sacrifice to remembering the giver rather than treating the animal as a power of its own. The provision belongs to Allah, so the ritual acknowledges His generosity and directs worship to Him.

phrases.translation: So eat from their meat and feed the desperately poor
phrases.explanation: People may eat from the sacrificial meat and are told to feed the desperately poor as well. The rite therefore includes both gratitude for provision and care for people in need. Sharing the meat prevents worship from becoming a private display and makes generosity part of the pilgrimage's practice.

phrases.translation: Then let them groom themselves, fulfil their vows,
phrases.explanation: Pilgrims are told to groom themselves and fulfill their vows after completing the central rites. The instruction marks a transition from the consecrated state and reminds worshippers to keep commitments made to Allah. The verse joins outward preparation with responsibility for promises made in devotion.

phrases.translation: and circle the Ancient House.”
phrases.explanation: They are then to circle the Ancient House. Circumambulation is a central act of pilgrimage directed toward the sanctuary established for worship of Allah. The verse completes the set of rites by bringing pilgrims back to the House, where their movement expresses devotion rather than worship of the building itself.

phrases.translation: That is so. And whoever honours the rituals of Allah, it is best for them in the sight of their Lord.
phrases.explanation: Honoring Allah's sacred rituals is best for a person in the sight of their Lord. The verse treats reverence for worship as a sign of obedience, not as a means of showing off. Respecting the rites reflects awareness of God and should be rooted in sincere devotion.

phrases.translation: The ˹meat of˺ cattle has been made lawful for you, except what has ˹already˺ been recited to you.
phrases.explanation: Cattle are made lawful for people except for the restrictions already recited in revelation. The verse connects permitted food with divine instruction, so people should neither invent prohibitions nor ignore God's limits. Its practical guidance in daily life follows the discussion of sacrifice and worship.

phrases.translation: So shun the impurity of idolatry, and shun words of falsehood
phrases.explanation: People are commanded to shun the impurity of idolatry and false speech. The verse moves from lawful food to moral and religious integrity, warning against associating partners with Allah and against lying. Honoring the sacred rites therefore includes truthful speech and exclusive devotion to Allah.

phrases.translation: Be upright ˹in devotion˺ to Allah, associating none with Him ˹in worship˺.
phrases.explanation: Believers are called to devote themselves uprightly to Allah and associate no partner with Him in worship. The verse defines sincere faith as turning directly to God rather than dividing devotion among rival powers. It follows the warning against idolatry with a clear call to stand firm in monotheism.

phrases.translation: For whoever associates ˹others˺ with Allah is like someone who has fallen from the sky and is either snatched away by birds or swept by the wind to a remote place
phrases.explanation: Someone who associates others with Allah is compared to a person falling from the sky, snatched by birds or carried by wind to a remote place. The image conveys helplessness and ruin after abandoning the secure path of worshipping one God. The further the fall, the more exposed the person becomes.

phrases.translation: That is so. And whoever honours the symbols of Allah, it is certainly out of the piety of the heart
phrases.explanation: Honoring Allah's symbols comes from piety in the heart. The verse connects outward respect for sacred rites with inward reverence, so ritual actions are not merely empty gestures. Their true value depends on devotion to God and awareness of what the symbols represent in conduct.

phrases.translation: You may benefit from sacrificial animals for an appointed term,
phrases.explanation: People may benefit from sacrificial animals for an appointed term. The verse acknowledges their practical use before they are offered, rather than treating them as objects with independent sacred power. Their provision and permitted use remain within the limits established by Allah. The ritual remains worship.

phrases.translation: then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House
phrases.explanation: The place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House. The verse directs the pilgrimage rite toward the sanctuary and keeps the act connected to worship of Allah. The animal is a means of devotion, while the House marks the place around which the sacred rites are organized.

phrases.translation: For every community We appointed a rite of sacrifice so that they may pronounce the Name of Allah over the sacrificial animals He has provided for them.
phrases.explanation: Every community has been given a rite of sacrifice in which people pronounce Allah's name over animals He provides. The verse places the pilgrimage practice within a wider history of worship. Across communities, the animal is a gift from God and the rite is an act of remembrance, not a separate object of devotion.

phrases.translation: For your God is only One God, so submit yourselves to Him ˹alone˺.
phrases.explanation: The verse declares that the believers' God is one and commands them to submit to Him alone. The sacrifice is therefore tied to exclusive worship, not to competition among deities. The shared principle unites the rites: provision comes from Allah and worship belongs to Him.

phrases.translation: And give good news ˹O Prophet˺ to the humble
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to give good news to the humble. Their humility is the response expected from people who recognize Allah as the giver and submit to Him. The verse turns from the universal rite to those who receive its message with reverence and willingness to obey.

phrases.translation: those whose hearts tremble at the remembrance of Allah, who patiently endure whatever may befall them,
phrases.explanation: The humble are those whose hearts tremble when Allah is remembered and who patiently endure what befalls them. Their reverence does not disappear during hardship. The verse describes an inward faith that remains aware of God and steady through difficulty, rather than demanding that life always be easy.

phrases.translation: and who establish prayer and donate from what We have provided for them
phrases.explanation: They establish prayer and give from the provisions Allah has granted them. The verse joins worship with generosity, showing that devotion is expressed both toward God and toward people. Their possessions are understood as a trust from Allah, so they share rather than treating every gift as theirs alone.

phrases.translation: We have made sacrificial camels ˹and cattle˺ among the symbols of Allah, in which there is ˹much˺ good for you. So pronounce the Name of Allah over them when they are lined up ˹for sacrifice˺.
phrases.explanation: Sacrificial camels and cattle are among Allah's symbols and contain benefit for people. Worshippers pronounce God's name over them while they stand ready for sacrifice. The verse presents the animals as provision and a sign of worship, with the ritual centered on remembrance of Allah rather than the animal itself.

phrases.translation: Once they have fallen ˹lifeless˺ on their sides, you may eat from their meat, and feed the needy—those who do not beg, and those who do.
phrases.explanation: After the animals fall, people may eat their meat and feed the needy, whether they ask or do not ask. The instructions make sharing part of the sacrifice and include people whose need may be visible or hidden. The rite therefore joins remembrance of Allah with practical care for others.

phrases.translation: In this way We have subjected these ˹animals˺ to you so that you may be grateful
phrases.explanation: Allah has subjected these animals to people so they may be grateful. Their usefulness is not a reason for arrogance or careless treatment, but a reminder of the provision God has made available. Gratitude includes remembering the giver and using what He grants in the ways He permits.

phrases.translation: Neither their meat nor blood reaches Allah. Rather, it is your piety that reaches Him.
phrases.explanation: Allah is not reached by the meat or blood of sacrifice. What reaches Him is the worshipper's piety. The verse corrects any idea that a ritual offering benefits God materially and directs attention to sincerity, obedience, and reverence as the true purpose of the act.

phrases.translation: This is how He has subjected them to you so that you may proclaim the greatness of Allah for what He has guided you to, and give good news to the good-doers
phrases.explanation: The animals are subjected to people so they may proclaim Allah's greatness for the guidance He gave and bring good news to those who do good. Sacrifice is thus linked to gratitude and praise, not merely to food. The verse ends by honoring people whose actions respond faithfully to God's guidance.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah defends those who believe. Surely Allah does not like whoever is deceitful, ungrateful
phrases.explanation: Allah defends those who believe and does not love the deceitful and ungrateful. The assurance follows the instructions on worship and sacrifice, reminding believers that they are not left without God's care. Deceit and ingratitude stand against the sincerity and gratitude expected from those who trust Him.

phrases.translation: Permission ˹to fight back˺ is ˹hereby˺ granted to those being fought, for they have been wronged.
phrases.explanation: Permission to fight back is granted to people who are being fought because they have been wronged. The verse frames this permission as a response to aggression, not an instruction to attack people simply for disagreeing. It recognizes the injustice of being targeted and driven into conflict.

phrases.translation: And Allah is truly Most Capable of helping them ˹prevail˺
phrases.explanation: Allah is fully able to help the wronged prevail. The assurance places the outcome in God's hands and offers hope to people facing aggression. Their strength does not come from claiming divine status for themselves, but from relying on Allah, who has power to support those treated unjustly.

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who have been expelled from their homes for no reason other than proclaiming: “Our Lord is Allah.”
phrases.explanation: The people granted permission to resist are described as those expelled from their homes solely for saying that Allah is their Lord. Their displacement is presented as unjust because their only stated reason is faith. The verse grounds the defense of the wronged in this specific persecution.

phrases.translation: Had Allah not repelled ˹the aggression of˺ some people by means of others, destruction would have surely claimed monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which Allah’s Name is often mentioned.
phrases.explanation: If Allah did not restrain some people through others, monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques where His name is often mentioned would be destroyed. The verse portrays resistance as preserving places of worship across communities, not merely one group's buildings. It highlights the wider harm caused when aggression goes unchecked.

phrases.translation: Allah will certainly help those who stand up for Him. Allah is truly All-Powerful, Almighty
phrases.explanation: Allah promises to help those who stand up for His cause and affirms His power and might. The promise follows the account of worshippers expelled from their homes, assuring them that oppression does not have the final word. Their cause remains under God's authority, and victory is not beyond His ability.

phrases.translation: ˹They are˺ those who, if established in the land by Us, would perform prayer, pay alms-tax, encourage what is good, and forbid what is evil.
phrases.explanation: Those established in the land are described by their worship and public conduct: they perform prayer, give alms, encourage good, and forbid evil. The verse presents authority as a responsibility to serve God and uphold what is right, not as permission for pride or abuse. Their faith should shape community life.

phrases.translation: And with Allah rests the outcome of all affairs
phrases.explanation: The outcome of every affair rests with Allah. Even people given influence cannot control the final result independently of Him. The verse closes the description of responsible leadership by reminding rulers and communities that their actions remain under God's judgment and that ultimate success belongs to His decision.

phrases.translation: If they deny you ˹O Prophet˺, so did the people of Noah before them, as well as ˹the tribes of˺ ’Ȃd and Thamûd
phrases.explanation: If the Prophet's opponents deny him, the verse recalls that Noah's people and the tribes of Ad and Thamud rejected messengers before them. Their disbelief is not evidence against the message, since earlier prophets also faced denial. The reminder encourages patience and warns that rejecting guidance has consequences.

phrases.translation: the people of Abraham, the people of Lot
phrases.explanation: The people of Abraham and the people of Lot are added to the list of communities that denied their messengers. The verse places current opposition within a recurring pattern rather than treating it as something new. It invites listeners to learn from earlier rejection instead of assuming their own community is exempt.

phrases.translation: and the residents of Midian. And Moses was denied ˹too˺.
phrases.explanation: The residents of Midian denied their messenger, and Moses was denied as well. The verse continues the examples to show that rejection crossed different peoples and prophetic missions. The names are reminders of past communities, not a claim that every person in a later community shares their wrongdoing.

phrases.translation: But I delayed ˹the fate of˺ the disbelievers ˹until their appointed time˺ then seized them. And how severe was My response
phrases.explanation: Allah delayed the disbelievers until their appointed time and then seized them, and the verse asks how severe His response was. A delay is therefore not proof that wrongdoing is overlooked. The warning urges people to use the time they have to change before consequences arrive.

phrases.translation: Many are the societies We have destroyed for persisting in wrongdoing, leaving them in total ruin.
phrases.explanation: Many societies were destroyed for persisting in wrongdoing, leaving their settlements in ruin. Their fate warns that wrongdoing can bring an end even to established communities. The verse asks readers to look beyond present power and recognize that no society is protected from accountability simply because it is wealthy or influential.

phrases.translation: ˹Many are˺ also the abandoned wells and lofty palaces
phrases.explanation: Abandoned wells and lofty palaces remain as traces of people who once lived there. The contrast between an impressive building and an empty place invites reflection on how temporary worldly security can be. These remains are reminders of past destruction, not proof that the people who built them escaped judgment.

phrases.translation: Have they not travelled throughout the land so their hearts may reason, and their ears may listen?
phrases.explanation: People are urged to travel through the land so their hearts may reason and their ears may listen. Seeing the remains of past societies should lead to reflection, not mere sightseeing. The verse describes travel as an opportunity to learn from history and recognize the consequences of rejecting guidance.

phrases.translation: Indeed, it is not the eyes that are blind, but it is the hearts in the chests that grow blind
phrases.explanation: The real blindness is not in the eyes but in hearts within the chest. A person may physically see and hear yet refuse to understand what the evidence means. The verse identifies inward resistance as the deeper obstacle and calls people to let their hearts respond to what they witness.

phrases.translation: They challenge you ˹O Prophet˺ to hasten the torment. And Allah will never fail in His promise.
phrases.explanation: The opponents challenge the Prophet to hasten the punishment, but Allah will never fail to fulfill His promise. Their impatience does not make the warning false or give them control over its timing. The verse calls them to trust that what God promises will occur, even if it is not immediate.

phrases.translation: But a day with your Lord is indeed like a thousand years by your counting
phrases.explanation: A day with Allah is like a thousand years by human counting. The comparison reminds people that their sense of time does not set God's schedule. What seems long to human beings does not mean that the promised judgment is forgotten, so delay should lead to reflection rather than mockery.

phrases.translation: Many are the societies whose end We delayed while they did wrong, then seized them. And to Me is the final return
phrases.explanation: Allah delayed the end of many wrongdoers, then seized them, and all return to Him. The verse repeats the warning that patience from God is not approval of injustice. A community may continue for a time, but its final destination is accountability before the One who knows every deed.

phrases.translation: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “O humanity! I am only sent to you with a clear warning
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is instructed to tell humanity that he has been sent only as a clear warner. His task is to convey the message and warn of its consequences, not to force people to believe. The verse clarifies his role and makes the warning accessible beyond one local group.

phrases.translation: So those who believe and do good will have forgiveness and an honourable provision
phrases.explanation: Those who believe and do good will receive forgiveness and an honorable provision. The promise joins pardon for past wrongdoing with a generous reward from Allah. It offers hope to people who respond to the warning with faith and action, rather than despairing over their earlier failures.

phrases.translation: But those who strive to discredit Our revelations, they will be the residents of the Hellfire.”
phrases.explanation: Those who strive to discredit Allah's revelations will be residents of Hell. The verse contrasts them with the believers and good-doers in the previous verse. It warns against deliberately opposing revelation and treating the effort to suppress it as a harmless disagreement or a path without consequence.

phrases.translation: Whenever We sent a messenger or a prophet before you ˹O Prophet˺ and he recited ˹Our revelations˺, Satan would influence ˹people’s understanding of˺ his recitation. But ˹eventually˺ Allah would eliminate Satan’s influence. Then Allah would ˹firmly˺ establish His revelations. And Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise
phrases.explanation: Accounts of this verse preserve different explanations of what Satan influences when a messenger recites or wishes. The reader's translation focuses on the effect on people's understanding: Allah removes that influence and confirms His revelations. The verse affirms God's control over the message, while its debated wording cautions against presenting one report as the only possible reading.

phrases.translation: All that so He may make Satan’s influence a trial for those ˹hypocrites˺ whose hearts are sick and those ˹disbelievers˺ whose hearts are hardened. Surely the wrongdoers are totally engrossed in opposition
phrases.explanation: Satan's influence becomes a trial for people whose hearts are spiritually sick or hardened, and the wrongdoers remain deeply opposed. The verse describes the different responses to a test: some turn it into a reason to resist, while others seek the truth. It warns that inner hostility can distort how people receive revelation.

phrases.translation: ˹This is˺ also so that those gifted with knowledge would know that this ˹revelation˺ is the truth from your Lord, so they have faith in it, and so their hearts would submit humbly to it.
phrases.explanation: People given knowledge recognize that the revelation is truth from their Lord, believe in it, and submit to it with humility. Knowledge here leads to a response, not simply possession of facts. The verse connects understanding with faith and a softened heart rather than pride or argument for its own sake.

phrases.translation: And Allah surely guides the believers to the Straight Path
phrases.explanation: Allah guides believers to the Straight Path. Guidance is a gift from God that directs faith toward a sound way of living. The verse completes the contrast with those who resist revelation, showing that people who believe are supported in continuing along the path of obedience.

phrases.translation: Yet the disbelievers will persist in doubt about this ˹revelation˺ until the Hour takes them by surprise, or the torment of a terminating Day comes to them
phrases.explanation: The disbelievers remain in doubt until the Hour suddenly overtakes them or a day of terminating torment comes to them. Their uncertainty does not prevent the promised event from arriving. The verse warns against treating continued delay as safety and urges a response before the opportunity to change has passed.

phrases.translation: All authority on that Day is for Allah ˹alone˺. He will judge between them.
phrases.explanation: On that Day, all authority belongs to Allah alone, and He judges between the disputing groups. No earthly ruler or community will control the verdict. The verse settles the earlier disagreements by locating final judgment with the One whose knowledge and power are complete, beyond human challenge.

phrases.translation: So those who believe and do good will be in the Gardens of Bliss
phrases.explanation: Those who believe and do good will be in the Gardens of Bliss. Their reward follows Allah's judgment and contrasts with the humiliating punishment described next. The verse gives reassurance that faith and righteous deeds are not lost, even when believers face opposition in this life.

phrases.translation: But those who disbelieve and deny Our revelations, it is they who will suffer a humiliating punishment
phrases.explanation: Those who disbelieve and deny Allah's revelations will suffer humiliating punishment. The verse states the consequence directly, contrasting their fate with the Gardens promised to believers. It warns that rejecting clear signs is a serious choice and that worldly status cannot prevent the judgment Allah has decreed.

phrases.translation: As for those who emigrate in the cause of Allah and then are martyred or die, Allah will indeed grant them a good provision.
phrases.explanation: Those who leave their homes for Allah's cause and are then killed or die will receive good provision from Him. The verse honors their devotion without treating death itself as a reason to seek harm. Their departure and sacrifice are known to Allah, who promises them a reward beyond what they left behind.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is the Best Provider
phrases.explanation: Allah is the Best Provider. The statement grounds the promised reward in God's generosity, not in the resources of the place the emigrants left. Their trust is directed toward the One who can provide for them in the Hereafter and knows the sacrifice they have made.

phrases.translation: He will certainly admit them into a place they will be pleased with.
phrases.explanation: Allah will admit those emigrants into a place where they will be pleased. Their reward answers the hardships of leaving home and facing death or persecution for faith. The verse promises a lasting destination that brings satisfaction, rather than claiming that their journey will always be easy in this life.

phrases.translation: For Allah is truly All-Knowing, Most Forbearing
phrases.explanation: Allah is All-Knowing and Most Forbearing. He knows the emigrants' intentions and their circumstances, and He does not rush to punish those who oppose Him. These attributes support the promise of a fitting reward and remind people that God's judgment combines complete knowledge with patience.

phrases.translation: That is so. And whoever retaliates in equivalence to the injury they have received, and then are wronged ˹again˺, Allah will certainly help them.
phrases.explanation: A person who responds in proportion to an injury and is then wronged again will receive Allah's help. The verse recognizes a measured response to harm and assures the wronged of God's support. It does not invite revenge without limits, since the opening condition is equivalence to the injury received.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is Ever-Pardoning, All-Forgiving
phrases.explanation: Allah is Ever-Pardoning and All-Forgiving. The verse ends the promise of help with attributes that encourage restraint and repentance. Even when a person has been wronged, pardon remains a valued response, and God's forgiveness is greater than human efforts to settle every dispute and can heal broken relations.

phrases.translation: That is because Allah causes the night to merge into the day, and the day into the night.
phrases.explanation: Allah makes night merge into day and day into night. The cycle shows that light and darkness change by God's command, rather than by a power independent of Him. The verse uses this familiar order to point to divine control over the world and its repeated patterns.

phrases.translation: Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing, All-Seeing
phrases.explanation: Allah is All-Hearing and All-Seeing. He hears what people say and sees their actions, including what happens as the day and night pass. These attributes assure believers that God knows their circumstances and warn wrongdoers that nothing they do is hidden from Him at any moment.

phrases.translation: That is because Allah ˹alone˺ is the Truth and what they invoke besides Him is falsehood,
phrases.explanation: Allah alone is the Truth, while what people invoke besides Him is falsehood. The verse distinguishes the Creator from the objects or beings treated as rivals to Him. Their worshippers may claim they have power, but such claims cannot change the reality that only Allah deserves worship.

phrases.translation: and Allah ˹alone˺ is truly the Most High, All-Great
phrases.explanation: Allah alone is the Most High and All-Great. The verse concludes by affirming His majesty above everything people associate with Him. His greatness is not shared with created beings, and no rival power can challenge His authority or take His place as Lord of all creation.

phrases.translation: Do you not see that Allah sends down rain from the sky, then the earth becomes green?
phrases.explanation: Allah sends rain from the sky and the earth becomes green. The change from dry ground to living growth is a visible sign of the provision and renewal He gives. The question invites people to notice this process rather than treating fertile land as something that appears without a cause.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is Most Subtle, All-Aware
phrases.explanation: Allah is Most Subtle and All-Aware. He knows the hidden details of creation and acts with wisdom that may not be obvious to people. The attributes follow the sign of rain and growth, directing attention from what is visible to the Lord who sustains it.

phrases.translation: To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth.
phrases.explanation: Everything in the heavens and on the earth belongs to Allah. The verse states that all creation is within His ownership and authority, so no part of existence is independent of Him. This truth underlies the earlier signs and the call to worship Him alone.

phrases.translation: Allah ˹alone˺ is truly the Self-Sufficient, Praiseworthy
phrases.explanation: Allah is Self-Sufficient and Praiseworthy. He does not depend on creation, while all beings depend on Him, and He deserves praise for His gifts and perfection. The verse contrasts God's independence with human need and reminds people that gratitude is owed to their Lord every day.

phrases.translation: Do you not see that Allah has subjected to you whatever is in the earth as well as the ships ˹that˺ sail through the sea by His command?
phrases.explanation: Allah has subjected what is on earth to human use and made ships sail through the sea by His command. The verse presents land, water, and travel as provisions made possible by God. Human skill matters, but it operates within a world and order that people did not create.

phrases.translation: He keeps the sky from falling down on the earth except by His permission.
phrases.explanation: Allah keeps the sky from falling onto the earth except by His permission. The verse points to the stability of the world as another sign of divine care. It does not describe people controlling the heavens, but reminds them that the safety they experience remains dependent on God's will.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to humanity
phrases.explanation: Allah is Ever Gracious and Most Merciful to humanity. The verse gathers its signs of provision and protection into an account of God's care. People benefit from the earth and sea, and are kept safe by His permission, so they are called to recognize His mercy and respond with gratitude.

phrases.translation: And He is the One Who gave you life, then will cause you to die, and then will bring you back to life.
phrases.explanation: Allah gives people life, causes them to die, and will bring them to life again. The sequence places the whole human journey under God's power and supports the chapter's repeated promise of resurrection. Death does not end His authority or prevent Him from restoring people for judgment.

phrases.translation: ˹But˺ surely humankind is ever ungrateful
phrases.explanation: Humankind is described as ungrateful despite the gifts and signs Allah provides. The verse challenges people who receive life and provision yet deny the One who grants them. It calls readers to recognize their dependence on God and to respond to His care with faith and thanks.

phrases.translation: For every community We appointed a code of life to follow.
phrases.explanation: Allah appointed a code of life for every community to follow. The verse recognizes that communities have received religious practice and guidance, while the central call to their Lord remains. It tells the Prophet not to let opponents turn this matter into a long and fruitless dispute.

phrases.translation: So do not let them dispute with you ˹O Prophet˺ in this matter. And invite ˹all˺ to your Lord, for you are truly on the Right Guidance
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to invite people to his Lord, because he is truly on the Right Guidance. The response to disagreement is clear invitation, not abandoning the message or returning hostility for hostility. The verse affirms the Prophet's guidance while leaving people responsible for whether they accept it.

phrases.translation: But if they argue with you, then say, “Allah knows best what you do.”
phrases.explanation: When opponents argue, the Prophet is to say that Allah knows best what they do. This answer leaves their actions and intentions to God's knowledge rather than continuing a quarrel without benefit. It reminds both sides that disagreement does not remove accountability before the One who sees every deed.

phrases.translation: Allah will judge between you ˹all˺ on Judgment Day regarding your differences
phrases.explanation: Allah will judge between all people on Judgment Day regarding their disagreements. Human disputes may remain unresolved in this life, but no claim is beyond God's knowledge. The verse reassures the Prophet and his followers that final justice belongs to Allah, who knows the truth of every matter.

phrases.translation: Do you not know that Allah ˹fully˺ knows whatever is in the heavens and the earth?
phrases.explanation: Allah fully knows everything in the heavens and the earth. Nothing is outside His knowledge, including people's public acts, private intentions, and the events of creation. The verse grounds the coming judgment in God's complete awareness, so no deed or disagreement can be hidden from Him.

phrases.translation: Surely it is all ˹written˺ in a Record. That is certainly easy for Allah
phrases.explanation: Everything is written in a Record, and preserving it is easy for Allah. The verse assures readers that their deeds are not lost or forgotten before judgment. Recording all things poses no difficulty for the Creator, whose knowledge and power are not limited by human memory or effort.

phrases.translation: Yet they worship besides Allah that for which He has sent down no authority, and of which they have no knowledge.
phrases.explanation: Some people worship besides Allah what He has given no authority to worship and about which they have no knowledge. The verse exposes devotion built on neither revelation nor understanding. A belief does not become sound merely because it is inherited or popular. It needs truth from God.

phrases.translation: The wrongdoers will have no helper
phrases.explanation: The wrongdoers will have no helper. Those who choose false worship cannot rely on the objects they invoke to rescue them from judgment. The verse completes its warning by showing the consequence of turning away from Allah, the only One with authority to help or protect.

phrases.translation: Whenever Our clear revelations are recited to them, you ˹O Prophet˺ recognize rage on the faces of the disbelievers, as if they are going to snap at those who recite Our revelations to them.
phrases.explanation: When clear revelations are recited, rage appears on the disbelievers' faces, as if they might attack the reciters. Their reaction shows hostility toward the message rather than a reasoned answer to it. The verse exposes how anger can replace reflection when people feel challenged by truth.

phrases.translation: Say, “Shall I inform you of something far more enraging than that? ˹It is˺ the Fire with which Allah has threatened those who disbelieve. What an evil destination!”
phrases.explanation: The Prophet is told to ask whether they would prefer to hear of something more enraging: the Fire promised to those who disbelieve. The warning shifts attention from their present anger to the consequence of rejecting revelation. Hell is called an evil destination, urging them to reconsider before judgment arrives.

phrases.translation: O humanity! A lesson is set forth, so listen to it ˹carefully˺: those ˹idols˺ you invoke besides Allah can never create ˹so much as˺ a fly, even if they ˹all˺ were to come together for that.
phrases.explanation: The idols invoked besides Allah cannot create even a fly, even if they all joined together. The example uses a tiny creature to make the failure of their supposed power unmistakable. Those who worship idols should reflect on the difference between the Creator, who gives life, and objects unable to create.

phrases.translation: And if a fly were to snatch anything away from them, they cannot ˹even˺ retrieve it from the fly.
phrases.explanation: If a fly takes something from the idols, they cannot retrieve it from the fly. The verse shows their helplessness in a simple, concrete situation. Their inability to recover what is taken makes clear that they cannot provide protection or benefit to the people who call upon them.

phrases.translation: How powerless are those who invoke and those invoked
phrases.explanation: The verse asks how powerless both those who invoke and those invoked really are. The worshippers lack a true source of help, while the idols cannot answer or act. The question invites people to abandon false dependence and turn their worship toward Allah, who alone creates and sustains.

phrases.translation: They have not shown Allah the reverence He deserves.
phrases.explanation: People have not shown Allah the reverence He deserves. The verse rebukes any worship or conduct that treats the Creator as though He were weak or comparable to created things. Proper reverence means recognizing His greatness and directing worship to Him, not to powerless idols or imagined partners.

phrases.translation: Surely Allah is All-Powerful, Almighty
phrases.explanation: Allah is All-Powerful and Almighty. His power is beyond comparison with the false gods that people invoke, and no one can prevent His judgment. The verse places the rebuke within an affirmation of God's strength, calling people to worship the One whose authority is complete.

phrases.translation: Allah selects messengers from both angels and people,
phrases.explanation: Allah selects messengers from among angels and people. The verse emphasizes that the choice of who conveys His message belongs to God, not to those who demand a messenger of their own preference. Both kinds of messenger serve by His selection and authority in conveying revelation.

phrases.translation: for Allah is truly All-Hearing, All-Seeing
phrases.explanation: Allah is All-Hearing and All-Seeing. He hears what people say about His messengers and sees how they respond to revelation. The attributes explain why He alone can select messengers wisely and judge their reception, since no hidden objection or action escapes His knowledge or sight.

phrases.translation: He knows what is ahead of them and what is behind them.
phrases.explanation: Allah knows what is ahead of the messengers and what is behind them. Their knowledge does not encompass everything, while God's knowledge includes their circumstances and what lies beyond their sight. The verse places even chosen messengers within dependence on the One who sent them.

phrases.translation: And to Allah ˹all˺ matters will be returned ˹for judgment˺
phrases.explanation: All matters will be returned to Allah for judgment. The verse follows the affirmation of His knowledge with the assurance that every affair ultimately comes before Him. People should therefore take their choices seriously, since no dispute or deed remains outside God's final authority at any time.

phrases.translation: O believers! Bow down, prostrate yourselves, worship your Lord, and do ˹what is˺ good so that you may be successful
phrases.explanation: Believers are commanded to bow, prostrate, worship their Lord, and do good so they may succeed. The verse brings physical worship and ethical action together. Success is linked to devotion and goodness, not merely to belonging to a community or performing outward acts without sincere obedience.

phrases.translation: Strive for ˹the cause of˺ Allah in the way He deserves, for ˹it is˺ He ˹Who˺ has chosen you,
phrases.explanation: Believers are called to strive for Allah with the devotion He deserves, and are reminded that He chose them. Their effort is a response to God's call, not a reason for self-importance. The verse presents faith as an entrusted responsibility and asks believers to commit themselves wholeheartedly to its cause.

phrases.translation: and laid upon you no hardship in the religion—the way of your forefather Abraham.
phrases.explanation: Allah has placed no unbearable hardship in the religion and identifies this way with the faith of Abraham. The verse reassures believers that worship is not meant to make devotion impossible. It calls them to follow the monotheistic path passed down through Abraham while remaining mindful of God's ease and guidance.

phrases.translation: ˹It is Allah˺ Who named you ‘the ones who submit’ ˹in the˺ earlier ˹Scriptures˺ and in this ˹Quran˺, so that the Messenger may be a witness over you, and that you may be witnesses over humanity.
phrases.explanation: Allah named the believers those who submit in earlier Scriptures and in the Quran, so the Messenger may witness over them and they may witness over humanity. The verse describes a responsibility to bear witness to guidance, not a license to claim superiority. Their testimony should reflect the message they have received.

phrases.translation: So establish prayer, pay alms-tax, and hold fast to Allah.
phrases.explanation: Believers are told to establish prayer, give alms, and hold firmly to Allah. These practices unite worship, generosity, and reliance on God. The verse closes its practical instructions by directing people to remain attached to their Lord, rather than placing ultimate trust in their own strength or possessions.

phrases.translation: He ˹alone˺ is your Guardian. What an excellent Guardian, and what an excellent Helper
phrases.explanation: Allah alone is the believers' Guardian, and the verse praises Him as the excellent Guardian and Helper. The closing words offer reassurance after the call to strive and worship. People who rely on God have a protector whose help is better than any created support.
